title: Flatness of normalized integral-to-native coefficient extension
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite field extension and $i:E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embedding. Use the native abelian coefficient ring $A_X$, its reconstructed section-ring sheaf, and any normalized coefficient presentation $C$ for $(E,i)$ of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data], with the specified commutative monoid structure. The ordinary extension of module sheaves along $C.\mathrm{integralMap}$, as defined in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], preserves finite limits. No constructibility or boundedness condition on its input module is assumed.

proof.text: Use the integral isomorphism of C and its residue normalization to put the completed coefficient into the continuous integral chart. The integral-inclusion and localization normalizations identify its rationalization with the actual continuous inclusion. Exact continuous localization and its ordinary section-action comparison give finite-limit preservation for this factor.

Identify i(E) with its finite intermediate field in the algebraic closure, using the algebra isomorphism induced by the injective field embedding i. Transport the finite-field chart along this isomorphism. The rational normalization of C identifies its rational inclusion, on each section and point, with this finite-field inclusion followed by the native coefficient comparison. Extension from this finite field to the locally finite algebraic closure is exact by the condensed coefficient calculus.

Under the section-module equivalences, restriction uses exactly the scalar maps just identified. The internal-section scalar-adjunction comparison therefore identifies ordinary extensions, with balanced generator b tensor m sent to itself. Compose the two exact extensions and the integral ring-isomorphism extension. The balanced tensor associator identifies the composite with pbcExtend(C.integralMap), proving finite-limit preservation. Zero modules and the empty scheme obey the same adjunction identities.

theorem nativeIntegralCoefficient_flat
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    [IsCommMonObj (abRing l X)]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (i : E →ₐ[Padic l] PadicAlgCl l) (C : CoefficientPresentation l X E i) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (pbcExtend (C.integralMap l X))
